subject: Cross-border capacity request — Horizon launch (EMEA & APAC)
messages:
From: Erin Wu <erin.wu@horizon.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial capacity ask: Horizon launch (EMEA + APAC)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking a look. We're planning to launch a new realtime feature for Horizon Analytics aimed at financial analysts in EMEA and APAC in Q4. We're running a limited pilot with 50 customers in July and expect a wider rollout in October if pilot KPIs hold.

High-level ask: can Redwood support a dedicated footprint across EMEA (Frankfurt) and APAC (Singapore) with a burst lane to US resources? We need an initial sizing recommendation and a rough cost delta between sustained reserved pool vs. burst-first model.

Quick details we have today:
- Expected monthly active inference requests (post-pilot): ~18M calls/month across both regions
- Target p95 latency: <350ms for generation (important for analyst workflow)
- Model family: 7B-13B LLaMA-style variants (we may push some traffic to a quantized 13B)
- Peak concurrency estimate (pilot->prod): 220 -> 1,200 concurrent in a peak 10-min window

I've attached our traffic expectation spreadsheet. Can you advise on a recommended pool split and suggested GPU classes (A100/A10? 80GB vs 40GB) plus a simple go-live timeline? Procurement will need an order-of-magnitude cost and a PO-ready SOW.

Appreciate it —
Erin

Attachments: capacity_expectations_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Erin Wu
Head of Platform Products, Horizon Analytics
erin.wu@horizon.ai
+65 9123 4567
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Wu <erin.wu@horizon.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: Horizon launch (EMEA + APAC)

Hi Erin,

Thanks — this is helpful. Looping in Ben from Capacity Planning and Laura on onboarding. High level: we can serve this with a tri-region approach (regional pools + burst lanes) that keeps p95 latency below your target if we combine modest reserved capacity with dynamic burst.

To produce a tight sizing/CAPEX vs OPEX delta, Ben and I need a couple of clarifications (listed so procurement can consume them directly):
1) Token profile: average tokens generated per call and 95th pct tokens (approx)
2) Percent of traffic requiring the heavier 13B model vs lighter 7B (even rough split is fine)
3) Whether data residency requires strict region-only routing for any customers (affects burst fallback)
4) SLO tolerance for graceful degradation (e.g., can we route to a lower-capacity quantized variant during burst?)

For transparency, I've attached a quick node calc with assumptions I asked Ben to sketch out. Ben — can you propose a baseline split and show both reserved-only and reserved+burst options?

Proposed next steps:
- Ben to deliver sizing + rough cost delta by EOD Thurs (11th)
- We recon with Erin and procurement on Fri to align on PO timelines and SOW items

Rafael Mendes
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Erin Wu <erin.wu@horizon.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T14:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: Horizon launch (EMEA + APAC)

Rafael / Erin,

Following up with an initial sizing sketch based on the traffic in Erin's sheet and Rafael's assumptions. Numbers below are conservative to preserve latency SLOs and allow for rolling upgrades. Assumptions: 13B quantized runs ~0.6-0.8x of 40GB A100 token throughput when using Redwoodatching + KV caching; 7B runs ~2-3x throughput. We recommend dedicated regional pools to keep tail latency predictable.

SIZING (baseline reserved vs reserved+burst):
- APAC (Singapore): Reserved baseline: 24 x A100-40GB equivalent (can be run as 48 x A10G-equivalents). Burst lane: +12 A100-equivalents during launch windows.
- EU (Frankfurt): Reserved baseline: 18 x A100-40GB equivalent. Burst lane: +8 A100-equivalents.
- US (fallback/burst only): No reserved capacity initially; maintain a lightweight pool of 8 burst-only A100-equivalents for overflow and emergency fallback.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: stage traffic 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 72h per region; require a canary rollback hook at 15% error/latency regression.
- Quantization profile: Use INT4 for non-critical inference to reduce memory and boost throughput; reserve INT8/FP16 for highest-quality flows.
- Autoscaling: aggressive burst policy for first 30 days (short cooldown) while we tune batch windows and prefix caching.

Rough cost delta (monthly committed unit estimates):
- Reserved-only (monthly equivalent nodes): APAC 24, EU 18, US 0 = baseline committed cost.
- Reserved+burst: same committed plus burst credit usage (we estimate 20-35% more in month 1 while traffic ramps). I'll attach a CSV with node-by-node math.

Attachments: hzn_initial_node_calc.csv, gpu_profile_options.pdf

Ben Carter
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Wu <erin.wu@horizon.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Horizon Analytics Procurement <procurement@horizon.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: Horizon launch (EMEA + APAC)

Thanks Erin and Ben — this looks good and actionable. Erin: based on Ben's sketch, the simplest commercial path we recommend is a 12-month reserved commitment for the APAC and EU baseline with an explicit burst allowance for months 1-3 to cover launch volatility. That gives you stable unit economics while preserving burst capacity to hit the pilot/promo spikes.

Next steps I'd like to propose (timeline):
- Tue 2028-06-18: Redwood sends a SOW + cost worksheet (procurement-friendly) with the two options (reserved-only vs reserved+burst).
- Wed 2028-06-20: 30-min procurement review to confirm billing cadence and PO language (we'll include SLAs and rollback triggers).
- Target canary start in region (APAC) by 2028-07-08 contingent on signed PO and initial onboarding checklist.

For procurement: I'll circulate a DocuSign SOW (link below) and a short appendix that lists allowed fallback behavior for regionally-restricted customers. If you need a formal SOC2/data residency clause included in SOW now, flag it and Laura will add the compliance appendix.

DocuSign (preview): https://app.docusign.com/pack/FAKE-DOCUSIGN-HZN-9731
Drive (supporting calc): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-horizon-capacity-plan

Erin — can procurement confirm target PO date? If you confirm PO timeline, we'll put the canary window on the calendar and reserve the burst lane capacity in advance.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
